speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance and sensation of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and how long it has been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash involve the diaper area or other body folds, and have you noticed any itching or cradle cap on the scalp? Is there a family history of eczema or asthma in addition to the father's psoriasis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the greasy yellow scales and distribution on the scalp and forehead, this presentation is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, often referred to as cradle cap in infants. I will now confirm this clinical assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic dermatitis
